basic_profile.name: Rajeev Nayar
basic_profile.headline: CDAO & Chief AI Officer | Built Products, Founded Practices, Scaled to $1.3B | GenAI · Governance · FinOps | 5 Patents | Stanford GSB
basic_profile.summary:
I've spent 30 years building things — not just leading them. The first half of my career I built software products: supply chain engines at i2, performance modeling tools at Hyperformix, a visual programming environment that predated low-code by a decade. The second half I brought that product-builder instinct into services — founding practices from zero, inventing frameworks, filing patents, and scaling a $400M Data & AI business to $1.3B.
Most CDAOs come from one world. I've operated in both, which changes how I approach transformation: I don't just buy or integrate technology, I know how to build it.
Here's what that looks like at scale:

• At Infosys, I grew the Data & Analytics unit from $400M to $1.3B (22% CAGR) — leading a geographically dispersed 1,400-person organization across 10+ countries and personally owning Data & AI architecture for contracts from $120M to multi-billion dollar global engagements.

• I designed "Boundary-less Data" — an early lakehouse architecture that increased enterprise data adoption by 300% and reduced one client's projected $300M data spend to $85M (71% savings) through Data FinOps controls.

• I built the governance layer that makes AI trustworthy. My "Governance by Exception" model took data trust scores from 30% to 85% at a Fortune-class beverage company.

• I founded Infosys's Big Data practice from zero to $44M, invented and patented "Big Data Edge," and built an MDM practice from $0 to $25M. Before that, I built an MDM product at i2 that was later acquired by Teradata.

At Tiger Analytics, I was hired to scale partner-led revenue from 2% to 25% in 3 years. In under a year we reached 15% — ahead of plan — and built the M2M partner pipeline to $35M.

What a product-builder brings to a CDAO seat:
• I build frameworks, not just strategies — Boundary-less Data, Governance by Exception, Big Data Edge are named, patented, and proved at scale.

• I speak engineer and CFO — Stanford GSB + MSEE in Computer Engineering.

• I generate IP, not just consume it — 5 patents, one product exit (Teradata acquisition).

• I move at product speed — practices built from $0 to $25M–$44M, partnerships from 2% to 15% in under a year.

I build organizations the same way — 1,400 people across 10+ countries, each accountable, each empowered to experiment and fail fast. That culture became a model adopted across Infosys.

Open to CDAO, Chief AI Officer and CDO conversations where building — not just buying — is part of the mandate.
Reach me at rnayar@yahoo.com. I respond to every thoughtful message.

basic_profile.name: Nishanky Gyanchandani
basic_profile.headline: AWS Partner Sales Manager at Tiger Analytics
basic_profile.summary:
I come from a strong technical background, starting my career as a Python developer and later working as a Generative AI developer, building solutions grounded in real customer and business problems.

During my time at Persistent Systems, I was deeply involved in multiple Generative AI initiatives, including developer productivity tools, observability chatbots, and enterprise-ready AI assistants powered by LLMs. These experiences strengthened my understanding of how AI can drive efficiency, automate workflows, and create tangible business impact.

Alongside my core work, I actively led and contributed to the AWS community at Persistent—driving knowledge sharing, enablement, and adoption of AWS and GenAI services across teams. This exposure helped me broaden my perspective beyond implementation and into ecosystem thinking.

Separately, I transitioned into working closely with the AWS partnerships team, where I supported go-to-market initiatives, joint solution development, and customer engagements. Being part of customer conversations—understanding their challenges, shaping solutions, and collaborating across teams—sparked my interest in growth, alliances, and business strategy.

Today, as Manager – Growth & Strategic Alliances at Oneture Technologies, I work at the intersection of Generative AI, AWS partnerships, and go-to-market execution. I focus on building scalable GTM motions, strengthening hyperscaler alliances, and enabling enterprise adoption of AI in collaboration with sales, product, and delivery teams.

I’m passionate about bridging deep technology with business outcomes, enabling responsible AI adoption, and building long-term partnerships within the AWS ecosystem.

past.employer_linkedin_description: Focaloid builds AI for manufacturers that pays for itself: decided on real numbers, built in about half the hands-on effort, and governed the whole way. We work with automotive, chemical, refinery and industrial manufacturers on the problems that sit between the plant floor and the business: test-order planning and production-line configuration, supplier risk, safe operating limits for plant equipment, master data across plants and product lines, and service workflows for CNC machines, robots and lasers. How we work: Accountable: an AI Business Case that puts a clear number on every AI idea before anyone writes code. Build cost, running cost, governance cost and savings, all traced to your data and signed off by a named consultant. Accelerated: our AI SDLC has agents write requirements, code and tests while a person approves every step. One requirement ID connects the business goal to the running system. Governed: a nine-phase governance lifecycle with documented go/no-go gates and signable evidence mapped to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001, built for safety-critical environments. What we deliver: agentic AI and copilots, production agents on governed data in Databricks and Snowflake, data engineering, IoT development and integration, and product, cloud and platform engineering. Since 2013: 200+ clients across the Europe, US, and Singapore, including a six-year run with a Fortune 500 automotive safety supplier. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified. Databricks Partner, Snowflake Partner and member of the Claude Partner Network. Name one process. Book a 30-minute discovery call.

past.employee_title: Prinipal Agentic AI Engineer - Semantic Layer
past.employee_description:
1. Built a semantic layer that unifies structured and unstructured enterprise data — SQL warehouses, policies, and domain documents — into one conversational interface, instead of separate tools for data lookups vs. policy questions.
2. Designed a "virtual graph" architecture: transactional data stays in the warehouse (no duplication), while a graph database captures the relationships and decision semantics on top of it — Data Nodes, Business Nodes, and Decision Nodes linked by typed edges reflecting how the business actually reasons.
3. Modeled causality explicitly as a graph — Trigger → Decision → Action chains — so root-cause analysis is an auditable traversal over a decision tree, not a black-box LLM guess.
4. Orchestrated a multi-agent framework with specialized agents per domain (inventory, demand, supply, root-cause analysis, recommendation, conversational follow-up), each owning a bounded reasoning scope and its own graph/SQL tools.
5. Grounded NL-to-SQL in a semantic catalog of governed, previously-validated query patterns (vector + lexical retrieval), improving reliability over pure ad-hoc text-to-SQL generation.
6. Built a numeric-grounding and fact-verification layer — every number is traced to a deterministic computation over the full dataset, with an automatic verifier rejecting and re-querying any ungrounded claim before it reaches the user.
7. Applied it to a real operational problem — stockout prediction and mitigation — where agents traverse the causal graph to explain why a shortage is emerging and generate ranked, explainable mitigation recommendations, not just flat alerts.

Our dedicated teachers, behavioral health team, speech therapists, and paraprofessionals work collaboratively to create opportunity and independence in the lives of our students. This interdisciplinary team is a skillful problem solving group that instructs and guides students toward greater independence and self-reliance, enabling a path to a brighter future.  With campuses in Palo Alto and San Jose, we serve multiple school districts and charters throughout the Bay.  A WASC accredited school, AchieveKids is a learning organization, where all of our community learns and grows.AchieveKids believes in creating a path to a brighter future.  Success within our school and community is wonderful, but we need to strive for more, helping to create opportunity in the lives of our students beyond our doors.  AchieveKids creates a school culture of learning, growing, reflection, and individual and community improvement.  To accomplish this task, AchieveKids utilizes the Learning for Life goals. We work to create Awareness, to develop a sense of Advocacy, to nurture one’s Ability to learn, and to enhance an individual’s Agility.  We meet our kids where they are and we take our kids where they need to go.  Together we Achieve!

The Indian School of Business (ISB) evolved from the need for a world-class business school in Asia. basic_profile.name: Akshat Chandna
basic_profile.headline: PhD | Data Science | Machine Learning | Deep Learning | Petroleum Engineer | Reservoir Engineer | Geostatistics | Geomechanics
basic_profile.summary:
With an innate urge to analyze and look for data driven evidence to make even the tiniest decisions of my life, it was fitting when I finally found solace in the arms of data science and machine learning as my chosen career path forward. I am very curious and detail oriented by nature and love to learn about the constantly evolving technologies of the fast paced IT sector. Actually not just learn, but DEEP LEARN them. And yes just like coding and data science, I also love puns.

I have a very varied background, something I believe supports my claim of adaptability. I am currently working as a Data Scientist in retail space (Lowe's) in the forecasting team. My day to day activities entail time series analysis, statistical analysis, implementing and optimizing machine learning and deep learning models, big data analysis and data visualization to name a few.

However my recently completed doctorate at Penn State was in a completely different field: application of Machine Learning to the energy sector. My research entailed development of a new multiple point statistics algorithm to accurately map fracture networks in a reservoir. To circumvent high computational costs involved with explicit geomechanical modelling, I devised a new methodology to integrate reservoir physics in a stochastic sense by using Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, Boosted Trees and Neural Nets.

To top that off, my Master's research at SIUC focused on finding answers to Coal Worker’s Pneumoconiosis through laboratory experiments and Computational Fluid Dynamics modeling of the flow of coal dust particles in turbulent mine airflow systems. I was also a member of an inter-departmental team that developed and analyzed a new Micro-Emulsion Technology for 12-15% more effective coal dust suppression to meet MSHA standards in coal mines.

I sincerely believe that the neural nets in my brain have learnt a lot from these past experiences, but the weights will continue to be updated with every learning opportunity I get. If you have any data science or machine learning opportunity, please do contact me at:

akshatch@gmail.com

I don't just build models; I build data products that solve ambiguous business problems at scale.

My expertise lies in transforming "what if" questions into deployed AI solutions—ranging from GenAI-powered knowledge assistants to large-scale causal inference engines.

Currently, at Tiger Analytics, I partner with C-suite leaders in Retail, Energy, and Healthcare to define product roadmaps and drive multi-million dollar revenue impact. I specialize in moving beyond the "POC trap" to deliver production-grade systems that stakeholders trust and use daily.

GenAI & LLMs: Architecting RAG systems and Agentic workflows (LangChain, RLHF) that solve real user pain points.

Product Strategy: Translating business goals into technical KPIs (North Star Metrics) and measuring impact via A/B testing.

Causal Inference & Optimization: Answering "Why" usage dropped or "How" to optimize margins using deep learning and integer programming.

I am passionate about mentoring data teams and driving the adoption of engineering rigor in data science.

past.employer_linkedin_description: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) was founded in 1909 as a result of the joint efforts of Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata, the Government of India, and the Maharaja of Mysore. In 1886, Jamsetji Tata conceived of a university of science that would work for the benefit of India, and in 1898 created an endowment for establishing such an institution. The Government of India then took up the effort, and, in consultation with scientists in England and in India, decided to locate the Institute in Bengaluru, where the Maharaja of Mysore, Shri Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, donated 372 acres of land. The Institute was formally vested in 1909, the foundation stone was laid in 1911, and the first batch of students started their studies in the same year.Over the last century, IISc has become the premier institute for advanced scientific and technological research and education in India. Beginning with 2 departments and 21 students in 1911, today IISc has 39 departments, units, or centres, 3500 students, and about 500 academic and scientific staff, supported by 600 administrative personnel. About 2200 students are in various PhD programs, almost 900 are enrolled for various Masters degrees, whereas about 400 are registered in the newly established, research oriented, four-year Bachelor of Science (Research) programme.In recent years, the Institute has vigorously promoted interdisciplinary research. New centres such as the CiSTUP, the Robert Bosch Centre for Cyber Physical Systems and a new Centre for Brain Research (funded by a large private endowment) are expected to conduct translational research in their respective areas, in order to better connect with industry and society. With the recent construction of modern buildings, acquisition of new research facilities, and induction of a large number of new faculty members, the Institute can look forward to an era of high productivity, increasing impact, and rising prominence in the world.

past.employer_linkedin_description: Indian Institute of Technology Madras is one among the foremost institutes of national importance in higher technological education, basic and applied research. In 1956, the German Government offered technical assistance for establishing an institute of higher education in engineering in India. The first Indo-German agreement in Bonn, West Germany for the establishment of the Indian Institute of Technology at Madras was signed in 1959.The Institute was formally inaugurated in 1959 by Prof. Humayun Kabir, Union Minister for Scientific Research and Cultural Affairs. The IIT system has sixteen Institutes of Technology. The first of these to be instituted are at Kharagpur (estb. 1951), Mumbai (estb. 1958), Chennai (estb. 1959), Kanpur (estb. 1959), Delhi (estb. 1961), Guwahati (estb. 1994) and Roorkee (estb. 1847, joined IITs in 2001).IIT Madras is a residential institute with nearly 550 faculty, 8000 students and 1250 administrative & supporting staff and is a self-contained campus located in a beautiful wooded land of about 250 hectares. It has established itself as a premier centre for teaching, research and industrial consultancy in the country.The Institute has sixteen academic departments and a few advanced research centres in various disciplines of engineering and pure sciences, with nearly 100 laboratories organised in a unique pattern of functioning. A faculty of international repute, a brilliant student community, excellent technical & supporting staff and an effective administration have all contributed to the pre-eminent status of IIT Madras. The campus is located in the city of Chennai, previously known as Madras. Chennai is the state capital of Tamilnadu, a southern state in India.

past.employer_linkedin_description: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) was founded in 1909 as a result of the joint efforts of Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata, the Government of India, and the Maharaja of Mysore. In 1886, Jamsetji Tata conceived of a university of science that would work for the benefit of India, and in 1898 created an endowment for establishing such an institution. The Government of India then took up the effort, and, in consultation with scientists in England and in India, decided to locate the Institute in Bengaluru, where the Maharaja of Mysore, Shri Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, donated 372 acres of land. The Institute was formally vested in 1909, the foundation stone was laid in 1911, and the first batch of students started their studies in the same year.Over the last century, IISc has become the premier institute for advanced scientific and technological research and education in India. Beginning with 2 departments and 21 students in 1911, today IISc has 39 departments, units, or centres, 3500 students, and about 500 academic and scientific staff, supported by 600 administrative personnel. About 2200 students are in various PhD programs, almost 900 are enrolled for various Masters degrees, whereas about 400 are registered in the newly established, research oriented, four-year Bachelor of Science (Research) programme.In recent years, the Institute has vigorously promoted interdisciplinary research. New centres such as the CiSTUP, the Robert Bosch Centre for Cyber Physical Systems and a new Centre for Brain Research (funded by a large private endowment) are expected to conduct translational research in their respective areas, in order to better connect with industry and society. With the recent construction of modern buildings, acquisition of new research facilities, and induction of a large number of new faculty members, the Institute can look forward to an era of high productivity, increasing impact, and rising prominence in the world.

past.employer_linkedin_description: A journey that began 80 years ago in a corner of India and has since traversed the world. Uniting people from across countries, cultures, and customs over the years with a multitude of different dreams, there's power in an idea. An idea that gave rise to brands that stood the test of time, with partnerships it inspired, and the people who made it all happen. One idea that sparked a legacy - this is the story of Bajaj Auto. “Do what you think is best, but be the best in what you do.” - Kamalnayan BajajThese words embody the spirit of Bajaj Auto. From 1945 to today, from “Hamara Bajaj” to “The World’s Favourite Indian”- the most loved motorcycle brand in almost 80 countries, Bajaj Auto carries its rich legacy and unconventional thinking, with a penchant for staunch differentiation.This philosophy has helped us be No.1 or No.2 in over 20 countries with industry-leading EBITDA of ~20%. Some statistics that reflect our strength:•A Zero Debt 5.5 Billion Dollar Company•World’s largest three-wheeler and third-largest two-wheeler manufacturer•India’s Number 1 motorcycle exporter – 2 out of every 3 motorcycles exported are Bajaj•The largest exporter of Branded Goods – exporting over half of India’s two- and three-wheelers•Over 33% of revenue from International markets, with 15+ million motorcycles soldWith powerful brands, our spectrum ranges from Boxer in Africa to KTM in Europe, from Rouser in Latin America to Pulsar in India; our versatility is evident. International alliances with KTM, Husqvarna, and Triumph have ensured that our horizons are broadened.A pioneer in motorcycle technology, our R&D is world-class, with talent from all corners of the globe, with TPM being the prime mover of productivity for the last 25+ years. From lean manufacturing, we have now moved to lean engineering & lean marketing, which has led to globally competitive fixed costs.With ever-expanding plans to win over the world, the sun truly never sets on a Bajaj Motorcycle.

basic_profile.name: Rana S.
basic_profile.headline: Architect, Engineer & Strategist | Translating AI into Business Outcomes | Data Science → Agentic Systems
basic_profile.summary:
Data Science Machine Learning professional with over a decade of experience delivering high-impact AI solutions across healthcare, supply chain, telecom, energy, and media. My expertise spans predictive modeling, Generative AI (LLMs, RAG, LangChain and Agents), and scalable ML deployments on cloud (GCP Vertex AI, Gemini Pro/Flash), driving measurable business outcomes.Over the years, I have led the full lifecycle of ML solutions—from problem framing and prototyping to deployment and monitoring—ensuring model health, maintainability, and alignment with business strategy. Keen about leveraging data responsibly, recognizing its human and contextual nature, and advocating for its ethical application to deliver meaningful, business-relevant results.

𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐀𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬
✅ Quantified model health & risk mitigation in the DC carton volume forecasting solution to safeguard against concept drift—supporting North Star metrics of <20% overtime hours and ≥98% on-time shipment, while sustaining $1M+ in annual overtime savings.

✅ Built an LLM + RAG based email classification and entity extraction solution, improving customer service operations and saving $45K annually; implemented a performance monitoring pipeline that adapted to evolving communication patterns, ensuring sustained accuracy and business relevance in production.

✅ Currently spearheading an AI agent foundation project for supply chain—automating supplier contract review, OCR extraction, clause matching, and email drafting—accelerating procurement decisions.

✅ Earlier projects include churn modeling for a telecom major (2% churn reduction), digital solar plant forecasting showcased at IEEE Summit, predictive asset maintenance publicized at IoT World Congress and designing and developing industry assets targeted for prospective clients.

► Tech Skills: Machine Learning | Time Series Forecasting | Deep Learning | LLMs | RAG | LangChain | Vector DBs (pgVector, Chroma) | Scikit-learn | XGBoost | PyTorch | FastAPI | SQL | Tableau | Python | R | Airflow | BigQuery | Vertex AI | GCP

► Soft Skills: AI Mentorship | Problem Solving | Stakeholder Engagement | Solution Design | Agile Delivery. I thrive at the intersection of applied machine learning and business impact—designing solutions that are not only accurate but resilient, explainable, and scalable. While I enjoy contributing to my current role, I am also open to exploring new strategic opportunities where I can create scalable, impactful solutions.

The price and promo elasticity can then be used to optimize the price to generate more revenue/sales .

basic_profile.name: Senganal Thirunavukkarasu
basic_profile.headline: AI Engineering Leader · Computational scientist and engineering executive · Built ML Engineering practice at Tiger; now leading org-wide technology strategy
basic_profile.summary: My path has been a bit unconventional. I started in software engineering, felt pulled toward problems with a deeper scientific and analytical nature, and ended up doing a PhD in computational science — which gave me an unusual blend of research thinking and engineering pragmatism.I've spent my career building things at the intersection of those two worlds. At Enthought, I worked with R&D organizations in life sciences and geosciences — building scientific software and platforms that turned research ideas into production-grade systems. At Tiger Analytics, I joined to build an R&D group but saw a larger structural gap — the absence of strong engineering culture and capability in an otherwise fast-growing analytics firm. I pitched the case for building it, got the mandate, and grew the ML Engineering practice from a small founding team to 400 people — generating $20M in direct revenue while enabling Tiger's broader AI practice to scale into new capability areas across predictive modelling, computer vision, GenAI, and agentic AI platforms.What I've come to believe — and what has shaped how I build teams — is that most AI initiatives struggle to hold two things simultaneously: genuine technical depth and the engineering culture and foundations to sustain that capability in production. Organizations tend to collapse toward one or the other. The work I care most about is building environments where both are taken seriously — and increasingly, I'm interested in using AI itself as a lever to make engineering teams more capable, more productive, and better at learning.Outside of work, I'm an avid reader of science fiction, fantasy, and LitRPG — and remain genuinely fascinated by the application of computational science to hard real-world problems in healthcare, life sciences, climate, and education.

basic_profile.name: subhashish kumar satpathy
basic_profile.headline: Associate Principal @ Tiger Analytics | GenAI,AgenticAI, ML, NLP, Python, GCP
basic_profile.summary: Technical Architect | ML Engineer | AI Orchestrator​I spend my days wrestling large datasets into submission and convincing algorithms to be nice to people. After 10+ years in the ML trenches, I’ve seen more overfitting than a tailor during the holiday season. Turns out calculus is actually good for something other than gatekeeping.​Currently, I’m a behavioral coach for machines—architecting Agentic AI frameworks to teach computers how to run errands without having an existential crisis.​The Essentials:​GCP Certified: I know how to throw expensive computations at the cloud without setting off the fire alarms.​The Stack: Python, modern ML, and yes, I still remember how to write a for loop.​The Goal: Building systems that actually move the needle—whether it's fixing Healthcare workflows, streamlining FinTech, or untangling Supply Chains. Solving real-world friction is a lot more noble than just optimizing ad clicks for things nobody needs.​The Filter:I’m a firm believer that technology should be a lever for human empowerment, not a tool for social engineering. I have zero interest in "innovation" that treats humanity as a resource to be pruned or a biology to be monopolized.I don't build systems designed to own people; I build systems that solve the friction of living.

Established in 1949 by the Murugappa Group in collaboration with Tube Investments (UK), TI Cycles is the first bicycle company in India to change the cycle retail landscape, both in urban and rural areas. The first Hercules bicycle was rolled out in 1951 and four more brands were added to the portfolio – Phillips in 1959, BSA in 1964, Montra in 2011, and Mach City in 2015 – each adding a new feather in our cap. past.employer_linkedin_description: Indian Institute of Technology Madras is one among the foremost institutes of national importance in higher technological education, basic and applied research. In 1956, the German Government offered technical assistance for establishing an institute of higher education in engineering in India. The first Indo-German agreement in Bonn, West Germany for the establishment of the Indian Institute of Technology at Madras was signed in 1959.The Institute was formally inaugurated in 1959 by Prof. Humayun Kabir, Union Minister for Scientific Research and Cultural Affairs. The IIT system has sixteen Institutes of Technology. The first of these to be instituted are at Kharagpur (estb. 1951), Mumbai (estb. 1958), Chennai (estb. 1959), Kanpur (estb. 1959), Delhi (estb. 1961), Guwahati (estb. 1994) and Roorkee (estb. 1847, joined IITs in 2001).IIT Madras is a residential institute with nearly 550 faculty, 8000 students and 1250 administrative & supporting staff and is a self-contained campus located in a beautiful wooded land of about 250 hectares. It has established itself as a premier centre for teaching, research and industrial consultancy in the country.The Institute has sixteen academic departments and a few advanced research centres in various disciplines of engineering and pure sciences, with nearly 100 laboratories organised in a unique pattern of functioning. A faculty of international repute, a brilliant student community, excellent technical & supporting staff and an effective administration have all contributed to the pre-eminent status of IIT Madras. The campus is located in the city of Chennai, previously known as Madras. Chennai is the state capital of Tamilnadu, a southern state in India.

basic_profile.name: Prakash Arunachalam
basic_profile.headline: Chief Operating Officer | Board Member
basic_profile.summary: Prakash is a seasoned IT industry veteran with an impressive 32 years of  career marked by significant accomplishments in Digital CX Solutions, Automation, and AI, particularly in the Banking & Financial Services as well as Healthcare sectors. He has led a large business of over $200mn with over 2500 team members globally. Currently as President & COO of Servion, his journey with Servion stared in 2017 as CIO back then when the company was owned by Everstone Capital a Singapore based Private Equity firm which eventually was bought by EMK Capital in 2023. Having the trust of both the outgoing PE as well as the incoming PE who retained Prakash on his COO role is a testimony of Prakash’s executive leadership skills. In this COO role, he leads Delivery, HR, IT, SQA and other enablement functions. Prakash was instrumental in achieving remarkable outcomes: a 50% revenue growth and an astounding 200% increase in EBITDA in just two years to maximize the value of Servion's Services business. Recognizing his unwavering excellence and executive skills, Everstone Capital promoted Prakash to the role of President & COO in 2020. He played a pivotal role in strategically separating Servion's Services and product businesses, subsequently unlocking the Product business's inherent value through a successful sale to another Private Equity firm in 2022, post that he led the M&A deal with the bankers and prospective investors, ultimately resulting in the sale of the Services Business in 2023 to Private Equity firm EMK Capital a London based Private Equity firm. Prakash strategically diversified Servion's partnerships, forging alliances with major CX industry players such as Microsoft, Google, AWS, Cisco, Genesys, Ring Central, Nice, Verint, and several AI-driven product companies offering Cloud-based Omni Channel Digital Solutions, Speech Analytics, Predictive Analytics, Customer Journey Analytics, and Automation solutions .Before his tenure at Servion, Prakash served as the Global Delivery Head for Banking & Financial Services at Virtusa, managing a substantial $200 million business and leading a global team of 2500+ professionals. Over 4.5 years at Virtusa, Prakash, in collaboration with the executive leadership team, was instrumental in driving the company's growth from $150 million to an impressive $1 billion, which included the strategic acquisition of Polaris. His illustrious career includes Sales leadership role at Polaris in UK for 4 years and Program management roles in EDS for 10 years.

past.employer_linkedin_description: EDS was started in 1962 by H. Ross Perot.[1] Perot’s goal was to establish a company that offered high-end electronic data processing management personnel, along with the computer hardware, by targeting large corporations and by offering long-term contracts at a time when short-term contracts were the industry norm. The creation of Medicare in 1965 gave EDS an opportunity to enter government contracting, and by 1968 Medicare and Medicaid contracts provided about 25 percent of EDS revenues. By 1977, healthcare-claims processing accounted for nearly 40 percent of EDS revenues. In 1984, General Motors agreed to buy EDS for $2.5 billion. In 1996, GM spun off EDS again as an independent company, and then became one of its largest clients. On May 13, 2008, Hewlett-Packard Co. confirmed that it had reached a deal with Electronic Data Systems to acquire the company for $13.9 billion.[2] The deal was completed on August 26, 2008. EDS became an HP business unit and was temporarily renamed "EDS, an HP company". Ronald A. Rittenmeyer, EDS Chairman, President, and CEO, remained at the helm and reported to HP CEO Mark Hurd until his retirement.[3] As of 2008, EDS employed 139,000 people in 64 countries, the largest locations being the United States, India and the UK. It was ranked as one of the largest service companies on the Fortune 500 list with around 2,000 clients.

basic_profile.name: Kunal Chikhale
basic_profile.headline: Leadership Development | Business Development | Theatre | Journalism | EdTech
basic_profile.summary:
For over two decades, I’ve been exploring the worlds of Learning & Development, Business Development, Journalism, and Acting—each chapter teaching me something new about people, communication, and the art of learning.

From newsroom floors at NDTV to corporate corridors at Hutchison 3 Global Services (now Tech Mahindra), from pioneering startups like Bizpunditz and Knolskape to global learning platforms like Emeritus—my journey has been all about helping people and organizations learn, grow, and transform.

I’ve loved building and scaling learning businesses—driving business development for L&D services and edtech solutions that make real impact. What excites me most is designing experiences that stick—whether it’s a classroom session, an outbound adventure, an e-learning journey, or a powerful video-based story.

Grounded in adult learning principles and fueled by experiential methods, I aim to make every learning moment engaging, meaningful, and unforgettable. My Mass Media background ties it all together—helping me craft stories that educate, inspire, and connect deeply with every learner and stakeholder.

current.employer_linkedin_description: KNOLSKAPE is a global leader in HR technology, helping organizations become performance-ready through AI-powered experiential technology. Trusted by 400+ organizations across 75 countries and engaging 550k+ employees, KNOLSKAPE enables measurable capability-building across the employee lifecycle.Guided by the belief that performance is built, not taught, KNOLSKAPE combines immersive experiences, talent intelligence, simulations, AI roleplays, coaching, and analytics to help enterprises drive faster ramp-up, visible readiness, personalized development, and real on-the-job application.Its proprietary 4E Framework — Evaluate, Educate, Experience, and Enable — provides an integrated architecture to assess skill gaps, build knowledge, accelerate practice, and reinforce workplace impact.At the heart of KNOLSKAPE’s ecosystem is GENIE, its agentic AI performance readiness platform. GENIE helps enterprises create custom readiness solutions, orchestrate the right experiences at the right employee touchpoints, and track performance signals in the flow of work. Alongside Passport and All Access Passport, organizations can deploy existing experiential offerings, build new ones, and scale contextual learning in days, not quarters.KNOLSKAPE supports leadership, digital and AI, customer, organizational, domain, and role readiness across use cases such as managerial readiness, sales readiness, onboarding, culture transformation, frontline capability, succession, high-potential identification, and leadership development.Founded by Rajiv Jayaraman, KNOLSKAPE operates across Singapore, Malaysia, India, Indonesia, the USA, and the UK, and is trusted by leading global brands including Allianz, BMW, Deloitte, EY, HDFC Bank, HSBC, KPMG, Nestlé, Siemens, TCS, UBS, and more.

past.employer_linkedin_description: Dale Carnegie helps people from all walks of life become fearless, giving leaders the confidence they need to get the most out of life and work. The executive branch headed by the President, who is the Head of State and exercises his or her power directly or through officers subordinate to him.[1] The Legislative branch or the Parliament consists of the lower house, the Lok Sabha, and the upper house, the Rajya Sabha, as well as the president. The legal system as applicable to the federal and individual state governments is based on the English Common and Statutory Law. basic_profile.name: Kalyan Teja Maganti
basic_profile.headline: Co-Founder & Chief Product Officer | KNOLSKAPE | Helping Organizations Become Future-Ready Through Experiential Learning
basic_profile.summary:
- Passionate about creating impactful products and building effective teams.
- Product leader with about two decades of experience in developing technology products.
- Expertise in product creation, launch, and Go-To-Market (GTM) strategies.
- Skilled in defining and delivering high-quality products that provide significant business value to customers.
- Integral member of a founding team, involved in incubating and scaling a business, and achieving results with lean teams.
- Enthusiastic about developing experiential, game-like products in the talent development space.

As the Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer at KNOLSKAPE, I am passionate about transforming talent development through innovative experiential learning solutions, and have been instrumental in building an award-winning portfolio of products designed to future-proof organizations and enhance their workforce capabilities.
With over a decade of experience in product leadership, I specialize in defining and executing product strategy, driving vision, and managing the end-to-end life cycle of experiential simulation products in a fast-paced agile environment. My expertise lies in creating impactful products, launching them successfully, and devising effective Go-To-Market strategies.

I hold a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science Engineering and a Master's degree in Economics from BITS, Pilani. My journey has been driven by a commitment to excellence and a dedication to delivering high-quality learning experiences that bring significant business value to our clients.

basic_profile.name: Gautam Bandyopadhyay
basic_profile.headline: Co-Founder & CEO- Trustt (formerly Novopay)
basic_profile.summary:
Co-founded Novopay in 2014 and currently heading the Banking solutions vertical. Novopay is a rapidly growing Fintech company funded by Khosla Ventures. We have a retail network with over 60k active outlets & a GTV run-rate of well over $1.7 billion a year. Our cloud-based, core banking solutions are used not just internally but also in a fast-growing Indian banks. Currently hiring for tech and product roles.

Until 2017 end, I headed operations and product function as COO of Novopay and was responsible for Business Operations, Product Management & QA, Partner Strategy and Device Strategy functions. 

Prior to starting Novopay, I played several roles from Product Management, Consulting, Global deliveries to Head of Innovation at Finacle (Banking Product) unit of Infosys. Early 2009, an interaction with Mr Nandan Nilekani - entrepreneur and co-founder of Infosys, changed my perspectives. I started Finacle Innovation Hub and added two new products – Finacle Inclusion Solution and Finacle Digital Commerce (FDC). One of many successes is Airtel Money – 1st & the largest Mobile operator wallet of India - which uses FDC as the core platform. 

Specialities: Digital Lending, Digital Banking, Payments, Core Banking, Financial Inclusion, Digital Commerce, Mobile Payments, Mobile Commerce, Start-up, BFSI, Product Management, Team building, Management

past.employee_description:
